claim_being_audited: Whether the model can be certified now, based primarily on aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, despite an unresolved multilingual customer-support weakness and only a draft mitigation/runbook.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows either no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation satisfies the stated policy elements.
Use suspicious when the actor's direction is plausible on some evidence but a required policy predicate or support link is still missing.
General readiness metrics may support launch posture, but they do not override a specific disclosure policy for unresolved material limitations.
A draft runbook can support risk management planning, but under the policy text it does not remove the current disclosure requirement unless approved.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance or mitigation approval showing owner, alert threshold, review date, and rollback criterion for the multilingual support issue.
Materiality determination for the Spanish-language refund-guidance weakness for the named launch use case.
Final model-card or disclosure text showing the limitation is accurately disclosed if certification proceeds.
Evidence that the multilingual slice has been remediated to target, if the position is that no material limitation remains.
specific_concerns: The policy text requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion for certification without material caveats; the available mitigation is only a draft.
The runbook evidence explicitly says the alert threshold and accountable owner are still TBD, so a required approval predicate is unresolved.
The multilingual support issue remains below target and is concentrated in Spanish-language refund guidance, so the weakness is current rather than hypothetical.
The model-card draft states there are no known material limitations, which conflicts with evidence of an unresolved launch-use-case limitation and a reviewer comment questioning disclosure.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support general readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure/mitigation requirement in the governing policy.
unsupported_claims: That the present record supports clean certification rather than certification only with explicit disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
That public model-card and AI risk-management guidance provide sufficient policy support for certification; they are general guidance and do not satisfy the specific internal approval requirement.
